    <TD><B>3</B></TD>
    <TD>
    <B>Discontinued operations</B></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
In November 2002, the Company liquidated the Travel
Subsidiaries, which consisted of 135 stores, due to their large
operating losses. In accordance with SFAS&nbsp;No.&nbsp;144, the
Travel Subsidiaries were presented as a discontinued operation
effective November&nbsp;19, 2002, and the consolidated financial
statements were reclassified to segregate the assets,
liabilities and operating results of the Travel Subsidiaries for
all periods presented.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
In 2004, the Company recorded $0.3&nbsp;million in income from
discontinued operations representing the reversal of the 2004
balance of the discontinued operations liabilities, related to
lease termination and store closing costs, that were no longer
required. This resulted in $0.2&nbsp;million in income from
discontinued operations net of tax, or $0.01&nbsp;net income per
share.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
As of January&nbsp;28, 2006, and January&nbsp;29, 2005, there
were no assets or liabilities related to the discontinued
operations of the Company.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
In May 2003, the Company sold its Miami, Florida distribution
center for net proceeds of $2.5&nbsp;million. This facility was
an asset acquired in the Bentley&#146;s Luggage Corp.
acquisition. The net proceeds from the sale decreased cash used
by discontinued operations for fiscal 2003.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
In 2005, the Company separately disclosed the operating and
investing portions of the cash flows attributable to its
discontinued operations for fiscal 2003, which in prior periods
were reported on a combined basis as a single amount.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
In 2002, the Company adopted SFAS&nbsp;No.&nbsp;144. Whereby,
the Company determines, based on sales projections for certain
markets in which Wilsons Leather has stores, whether the current
estimate of the future undiscounted cash flows in these markets
would be sufficient to recover the carrying value of those
stores&#146; fixed assets. In those instances where the
undiscounted cash flows are not sufficient to recover the
applicable asset&#146;s carrying value, an impairment loss is
recorded to write down the assets to fair value. During 2005,
2004 and 2003, the Company&#146;s impairment testing did not
indicate any impairment. However, as discussed in Note&nbsp;2,
&#147;Reorganization and partial store liquidation,&#148;
accelerated depreciation was recorded for the liquidation stores
throughout the term of the liquidation sale.
</DIV>

    <TD>
    <I>Term B promissory note and senior credit facility</I></TD>
</TR>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
General Electric Capital Corporation and a syndicate of banks
have provided the Company with a senior credit facility, which
as amended, provides for borrowings of up to $150.0&nbsp;million
in aggregate principal amount, including a $25.0&nbsp;million
Term B promissory note and a $75.0&nbsp;million letter of credit
subfacility. With the completion of the sale of capital stock
(described below in Note&nbsp;10, &#147;Capital stock&#148;),
and the subsequent repayment of the
11<FONT style="font-size: 70%"><SUP>1</SUP></FONT>/<FONT style="font-size: 60%">4
</FONT>%&nbsp;Senior Notes in full at maturity during 2004, the
senior credit facility expiration date was extended to
June&nbsp;28, 2008, at which time all borrowings, including the
Term B promissory note, will become due and payable.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The Term B promissory note is collateralized by the
Company&#146;s inventory. The remainder of the senior credit
facility is collateralized by the Company&#146;s inventory,
equipment and credit card receivables. Through the third quarter
of 2005 interest on cash borrowings under the senior credit
facility was at the applicable LIBOR (seven to 30&nbsp;days)
plus 1.50%, the commercial paper rate plus 1.50% or the prime
rate plus 0.25%. Commencing with the fourth quarter of 2005,
interest is payable on revolving credit borrowings at variable
rates determined by the applicable LIBOR plus 1.25% to 1.75%, or
the prime rate plus 0.0% to 0.5% (commercial paper rate plus
1.25% to 1.75% if the loan is made under the &#147;swing
line&#148; portion of the revolver). The applicable margin will
be adjusted quarterly on a prospective basis based on
achievement of defined quarterly EBITDA targets. With respect to
the Term B promissory note, the interest rate in 2005 was the
prime rate plus 4.0%, plus an additional 2.75% pursuant to a
separate letter agreement with General Electric Capital
Corporation. On January&nbsp;31, 2006, the Company executed
another letter agreement with General Electric Capital
Corporation whereby the additional 2.75% is no longer
applicable. The Company pays monthly fees of 0.375%&nbsp;per
annum on the unused portion of the senior credit facility, as
defined, and 3.25%&nbsp;per annum on the average daily amount of
letters of credit outstanding during each month.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The senior credit facility contains certain restrictions and
covenants, which, among other things, restrict the
Company&#146;s ability to make capital expenditures; acquire or
merge with another entity; make investments, loans or
guarantees; incur additional indebtedness; create liens or other
encumbrances; or pay cash dividends
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The Company files federal and state income tax returns based on
a 52/53&nbsp;week year ending on the Saturday closest to
July&nbsp;31. As of the tax year ended July&nbsp;30, 2005, the
Company had federal net operating loss carryforwards of
$43.7&nbsp;million that expire in 2023 and 2024. In addition,
the Company had state net operating loss carryforwards that
expire at varying dates through 2024. The Company has not
recorded a tax benefit on any of the federal or state tax loss
carryforwards as a full valuation allowance offsets these assets.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The ability to utilize net operating loss carryforwards is
limited under various provisions of the Internal Revenue Code,
including Section&nbsp;382. The Company has determined that a
change in ownership under this section occurred on June&nbsp;4,
2003 resulting in $33.6&nbsp;million of the total
$43.7&nbsp;million net operating loss carryforward being limited.
</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">
<B>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 18pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
In evaluating the Company&#146;s ability to recover deferred tax
assets, the Company has considered all available positive and
negative evidence including; past operating results, the
existence of cumulative losses in the most recent fiscal years,
forecasts of future taxable income including the reversal of
temporary differences and the implementation of feasible and
prudent tax planning strategies. In light of cumulative losses
over the past five fiscal years, the Company believes that it is
more likely than not that the Company&#146;s net deferred tax
asset will not be realized. Accordingly, a full valuation
allowance has been recorded against the net deferred tax assets.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
During 2005, the Company identified a tax planning strategy that
allowed it to maintain a valuation allowance on its net deferred
tax assets inclusive of its tax basis LIFO reserve.
Historically, the Company&#146;s deferred tax liability related
to its tax basis LIFO reserve was excluded when determining the
amount of required valuation allowance. The result of this tax
planning strategy was the recognition of a deferred tax benefit
of $1.0&nbsp;million in 2005.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
As discussed in Note&nbsp;3, &#147;Discontinued
operations,&#148; the Company liquidated its travel business in
2002. By the end of the fourth quarter of 2004, the Company
determined that the accruals for store closing activities were
no longer required and included the remaining $0.3&nbsp;million
in income from discontinued operations, $0.2&nbsp;million net of
tax.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
On April&nbsp;25, 2004, the Company entered into an agreement to
issue 17,948,718&nbsp;shares of the Company&#146;s common stock
(the &#147;Equity Financing&#148;) to three institutional
investors at a price of $1.95&nbsp;per share. The transaction
closed on July&nbsp;2, 2004, with gross proceeds before offering
expenses of $35.0&nbsp;million. As additional consideration for
the investors&#146; commitment, on April&nbsp;25, 2004, the
Company issued two million warrants exercisable for five years
to the investors upon signing the Equity Financing agreement,
and at closing issued an additional two million warrants
exercisable for five years, all at an exercise price of
$3.00&nbsp;per share of common stock. All four million of the
warrants issued contain certain weighted average anti-dilution
rights as defined in the Common Stock and Warrant Purchase
Agreement. On July&nbsp;9, 2004, the Company repurchased
$22.0&nbsp;million of the
11<FONT style="font-size: 70%"><SUP>1</SUP></FONT>/<FONT style="font-size: 60%">4</FONT>%&nbsp;Senior
Notes with proceeds from the Equity Financing. The Company used
$8.6&nbsp;million of the proceeds from the Equity Financing to
repay the balance of the
11<FONT style="font-size: 70%"><SUP>1</SUP></FONT>/<FONT style="font-size: 60%">4
</FONT>%&nbsp;Senior Notes at maturity. The balance of the
proceeds have been used for general working capital purposes.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The relative fair value of the warrants and common stock sold,
determined using the Black-Scholes model, was allocated within
additional paid-in capital at closing. The Equity Financing
qualified as a &#147;change in control&#148; pursuant to the
Company&#146;s equity compensation plans. As such, vesting was
accelerated on all outstanding unvested stock options and
restricted stock as of July&nbsp;2, 2004.

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The Company accounts for its stock-based awards using the
intrinsic-value method. Accordingly, no compensation expense has
been recognized in the financial statements for employee stock
option awards granted at fair market value. However, beginning
in the first quarter of 2006, the Company will adopt the
fair-value method of SFAS&nbsp;No.&nbsp;123R whereby the Company
will be required to recognize compensation expense in an amount
equal to the fair market value of share-based payments granted
to employees.
</DIV>

<FONT face="helvetica,arial">

<DIV align="center" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff;">
<B>WILSONS THE LEATHER EXPERTS INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">
<B>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL
STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued)</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 18pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The Company&#146;s calculations are based on a single-option
valuation approach and forfeitures are recognized as they occur.
Had compensation cost for Wilsons Leather&#146;s stock option
plans been determined based on the fair value at the grant date
for awards from 1996 through 2005, consistent with the
provisions of SFAS&nbsp;No.&nbsp;123, the Company&#146;s net
income (loss) and net income (loss) per share would have
decreased/increased to the pro forma amounts disclosed in
Note&nbsp;1, &#147;Summary of significant accounting
policies.&#148;
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; color: #000000; background: #ffffff;"></DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff;">

<TR>
    <TD width="3%"></TD>
    <TD width="97%"></TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD></TD>
    <TD>
    <I>Restricted stock</I></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The Company has awarded restricted stock grants to selected
employees under the Amended and Restated 2000 Long Term
Incentive Plan. In March 2004 and 2003, 44,000 and
120,000&nbsp;shares of restricted stock were issued under this
plan, respectively. These restricted stock awards generally
vested ratably over four years from the date of grant, subject
to acceleration if certain performance targets were met. When
restricted shares are issued, deferred compensation is recorded
as a reduction of shareholders&#146; equity. Annual compensation
is charged to expense over the vesting period. As discussed in
Note&nbsp;10, &#147;Capital stock,&#148; the Equity Financing
qualified as a &#147;change in control&#148; pursuant to the
Company&#146;s Plans, defined above. As a result,
$0.7&nbsp;million of expense was recorded in July of 2004
related to accelerated vesting of the outstanding unvested
restricted stock as of July&nbsp;2, 2004. During 2004, and 2003,
$0.8&nbsp;million, and $0.4&nbsp;million was charged to expense
for vested restricted shares, respectively. There was no related
expense recorded in 2005.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; color: #000000; background: #ffffff;"></DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff;">

<TR>
    <TD width="3%"></TD>
    <TD width="97%"></TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD></TD>
    <TD>
    <I>Employee stock purchase plan</I></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The Company has an employee stock purchase plan that is
qualified under Section&nbsp;423 of the Internal Revenue Code of
1986. Employees are entitled to have payroll deductions withheld
that are used to purchase company stock at a 15% discount at
defined times during the year. The Company has allowed for
625,000&nbsp;shares of common stock to be purchased under this
plan. As of January&nbsp;28, 2006, 372,160&nbsp;shares had been
issued under the plan.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; color: #000000; background: #ffffff;"></DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff;">

<TR>
    <TD width="6%"></TD>
    <TD width="94%"></TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD><B>12</B></TD>
    <TD>
    <B>401(k) profit sharing plan</B></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The Company has a defined contribution 401(k) profit-sharing
plan for eligible employees, which is qualified under
Sections&nbsp;401(a) and 401(k) of the Internal Revenue Code of
1986. Employees are entitled to make tax deferred contributions
of up to 30% of their eligible compensation, subject to annual
IRS limitations. As of January&nbsp;1, 2006, for employees who
have worked more than one year, the Company matches 100% of
contributions, up to a maximum of 3.0% of the employee&#146;s
eligible compensation and 50% of contributions up to the next
2.0% of eligible compensation. These Company matching
contributions are 100% vested when made. Prior to
January&nbsp;1, 2006, for employees who had worked less than
three years but more than one year, the Company matched 25% of
contributions, up to a maximum of 4% of the employee&#146;s
eligible compensation and for employees who had worked more than
three years, the Company matched 50% of contributions, up to a
maximum of 4% of the employee&#146;s eligible compensation.
These Company matching contributions vest after three years of
service or upon death of the employee. Company contributions net
of forfeitures were $0.3&nbsp;million, $0.0&nbsp;million, and
$0.0&nbsp;million in 2005, 2004, and 2003, respectively. The
Company may also, at its discretion, make a profit-sharing
contribution to the 401(k) plan for each plan year. The
Company&#146;s profit sharing contributions vest after five
years. No profit sharing contributions were made during the
years 2003 through 2005.

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
In late September 2005, the Company became aware of a kickback
scheme involving its General Manager&#151; Asia and certain
vendors. On October&nbsp;4, 2005 the General Manager&#151; Asia
admitted that he had received kickbacks from certain vendors
over a period of eight years aggregating nearly
$4.0&nbsp;million. The General Manager&#151; Asia was terminated
and the Company&#146;s Audit Committee and outside auditors were
informed of the acknowledged kickbacks and the termination. On
October&nbsp;14, 2005, the Company&#146;s Audit Committee
retained outside counsel, and outside counsel investigated the
extent of the kickback scheme, whether other employees were
involved in or had knowledge of the kickbacks or similar
arrangements, and whether any violations of the Foreign Corrupt
Practices Act had occurred in connection with the kickback
arrangements.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The investigation by outside counsel did not indicate that any
employee other than the General Manager&#151; Asia was involved
in, or had previous knowledge of, the kickback scheme or similar
arrangements or that there were any violations of the Foreign
Corrupt Practices Act. The investigation also did not indicate
that the magnitude of the kickbacks exceeded, or were less than,
the nearly $4.0&nbsp;million acknowledged by the former General
Manager&#151; Asia.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
Subsequent to his termination, the former General Manager&#151;
Asia paid Wilsons Leather approximately $0.5&nbsp;million. The
Company has notified its insurance carrier of this issue and if
the Company is able to receive
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
During June 2002, the Company entered into an agreement for the
sale and leaseback of its corporate headquarters and
distribution center in Brooklyn Park, Minnesota, for net
proceeds of $12.5&nbsp;million. The initial term of the lease is
15&nbsp;years, with an option to renew for an additional
five-year period. The agreement includes an option for the
Company to buy out the lease at the end of the tenth year for a
price of $500,000. The lease is classified as an operating lease
in accordance with SFAS&nbsp;No.&nbsp;13, <I>Accounting for
Leases.</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The net book value of the building approximated
$3.1&nbsp;million and has been removed from the accounts. The
$9.4&nbsp;million gain on the sale has been deferred and the
appropriate amounts properly classified under short- and
long-term liabilities. The short-term portion is included in
&#147;accrued expenses&#148; and the long-term portion is
included in &#147;other long-term liabilities&#148; on the
balance sheet. Payments under the lease approximated
$1.4&nbsp;million for the first year, with an annual increase of
2.5% each year thereafter.

<TR valign="top">
    <TD><B>16</B></TD>
    <TD>
    <B>Subsequent events</B></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10.0pt;color: #000000; background: #ffffff; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0; ">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
On January&nbsp;31, 2006, the Company executed a Letter
Agreement with General Electric Capital Corporation (the
&#147;Letter Agreement&#148;) modifying certain fees related to
its senior credit facility. Under the Letter Agreement, the
Company is allowed to repay or prepay all or a portion of the
outstanding balance on its Term B promissory note prior to
July&nbsp;31, 2007, subject to a fee totaling 0.5% of the
principal amount repaid or prepaid. After July&nbsp;31, 2007,
the Company is allowed to prepay any remaining outstanding
balance without penalty. In addition, the January&nbsp;31, 2006,
Letter Agreement eliminates the additional 2.75% that was
applied to the interest rate on the Term B promissory note.
</DIV>
